texts: bad: the rule the translator built can never fire — its trigger is written in terms no recorded fact can ever match — so no apprentice is ever assigned to a station, and the thirty nights are also slotted as something the completing alters rather than as what gets completed. Your wording is not really the culprit: the same sentence with "ten" in place of "thirty" parsed cleanly, so this is a translator slip more than a phrasing problem. If you want to steer it, use the plainest trigger connective and keep the condition as one finite clause: "When an apprentice completes thirty solo nights, the Council assigns that apprentice to a station."

good. the trigger matches on ordinary variables, so each time an apprentice completes the ten solo nights the rule mints that apprentice's own assignment to a station, tied to the completion that set it off.
